Project Topic
In this project, we analyze the patterns and motivations behind internal migration in Türkiye by using officially published migration statistics from the Turkish Statistical Institute (TÜİK). Rather than focusing only on where people move, we aim to understand why these migration movements occur by examining factors such as educational opportunities, employment, housing conditions, marriage, retirement, and lifestyle preferences.
Using province-level migration data from all 81 provinces in Türkiye, we investigate how socio-economic differences between regions influence internal migration across the country. Through data cleaning, exploratory data analysis, and data visualization techniques in R, we explore migration flows, compare provinces, and identify the major drivers behind migration patterns.
Our project combines statistical analysis with visual communication to better understand how internal migration reflects broader social and economic dynamics in Türkiye. By transforming raw migration tables into an analysis-ready dataset, we aim to make migration data easier to visualize, interpret, and communicate to different audiences.

title: Data
text: To meet the project requirement of using a “real-world dataset connected to Türkiye,” we selected official statistics from the Turkish Statistical Institute (TÜİK). We focused on the most recent “Internal Migration Statistics” (2024) and specifically utilized the “Inter-provincial migration by reason of migration” tables.

title: Data
text:
2. Dataset Introduction
Our dataset details the migration movements across Türkiye’s 81 provinces based on 10 fundamental reasons:

Job Assignment / Change of Job
Starting a Job / Finding a Job
Education
Marital Status / Family-related Reasons
Better Housing and Living Conditions
Migration Dependent on a Household Member
Retirement
Earthquake (Special provision)
Health / Care
Other / Unknown
